blocks.text: [F] Vinati Organics is a Maharashtra-based B2B manufacturer of specialty monomers, aromatics, butyl phenols, antioxidants, polymers and inorganic intermediates, with more than 30 products (SCREENER). [F] It makes money by converting crude-linked feedstocks (toluene, propylene, acrylonitrile, MTBE) into intermediates sold to chemical, polymer and pharmaceutical manufacturers, largely under formula or cost-plus pricing that passes input costs through with a quarterly lag (RATING). [MC] Its two anchor molecules are ATBS (a sulfonic-acid monomer used in polymers for enhanced oil recovery, water treatment, detergents, mining and personal care) and IBB (the key intermediate for ibuprofen), in which it claims a global share of about 65% (AR2025 p.6). [F] FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs2,227 crore, EBITDA Rs655 crore (29.4% margin) and PAT Rs444 crore; the June 2026 quarter (Q1 FY27) delivered revenue of Rs696 crore, EBITDA of Rs170 crore and PAT of Rs109 crore (NUMBERS).

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. [F] Growth has stalled: three-year sales CAGR is 2.5% and FY26 revenue of Rs2,227 crore was below FY25's Rs2,248 crore (NUMBERS), against a 20% revenue CAGR guided for three years in August 2024 and May 2025 [MC] (CALL Aug 2024; CALL May 2025).

2. [E] Heavy capex has not yet earned its keep: capex over FY24-FY26 totalled Rs1,164 crore while sales rose only Rs161 crore and EBITDA Rs82 crore versus FY23 (NUMBERS); fixed-asset turnover fell from 1.78x in FY23 to 1.05x in FY26 (NUMBERS).

3. [F] Valuation is far above every scenario in our DCF model: price Rs1,206 against bear/base/bull per-share values of Rs176.5/Rs251.5/Rs306.4, and the reverse DCF implies ~137% annual sales growth for five years (NUMBERS).

4. [F] Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 24.4% on revenue up 28.4% year on year, below the 26-27% band management calls sustainable [MC] (NUMBERS; CALL May 2026); no explanation is in our evidence because no Q1 FY27 transcript was available.

5. [F] VOPL, a ~Rs500 crore project, produced turnover of only Rs10.55 crore and a Rs9.995 crore loss in FY25 (AR2025 p.215) and ~Rs10 crore of sales in FY26 [MC] (CALL May 2026), and now needs process re-engineering.

6. [F] Working capital is lengthening: inventory days rose from 68 in FY25 to 110 in FY26 and the cash conversion cycle from 118 to 152 days (NUMBERS); the FY25 report also states 13.60% of receivables were overdue beyond 180 days versus 0.21% a year earlier (AR2025 p.209).
7. [F] Product concentration: ATBS alone is about one-third of revenue [MC] (CALL May 2026), and its demand softened from October 2025, causing the full-year target to be missed [MC] (CALL May 2026).
8. [F] Antioxidants face Chinese undercutting and India's anti-dumping application was not accepted; management has reapplied and expects 6-9 months for any outcome [MC] (CALL May 2026).

9. [F] MD and CEO remuneration rose 287.4% to Rs9.11 crore in FY25, 164.67x the median employee (AR2025 p.44), in a year PAT grew 25% (NUMBERS); a further remuneration revision was approved at the September 2026 AGM (ANNOUNCEMENTS).
10. [F] Institutional sponsorship is thinning at the margin: FII holding fell from 5.48% (Sep 2024) to 3.65% (Jun 2026) and the stock is 34.8% below its 52-week high (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: [AI] The consensus framing of Vinati is a small-market monopolist with pricing discipline; our reading is that the franchise is real but the growth narrative has repeatedly run ahead of delivery. [F] Management guided a 20% three-year revenue CAGR in August 2024 (CALL Aug 2024) and FY26 revenue then fell slightly (NUMBERS). [F] VOPL was guided to ~Rs100 crore in FY26 (CALL May 2025) and delivered ~Rs10 crore [MC] (CALL May 2026). [AI] The investment debate should therefore shift from 'how dominant is ATBS' to 'what return does the Rs1,164 crore of FY24-FY26 capex earn' and 'why did Q1 FY27 margins compress on strong volumes'. [AI] At Rs1,206 the market is paying for a successful answer to both, which our DCF framework cannot corroborate (NUMBERS).

subsections.title: Export mix change: strategy or mix?

blocks.text: [MC] Management says exports fell from ~70% three to four years ago to ~55% as domestic AO, butyl phenol and IB sales grew (CALL May 2025). [MC] ATBS is 90-95% exported (CALL Aug 2024). [AI] The shift is mix-driven (growth of domestic-facing AO and IB) rather than a deliberate de-globalisation. [F] Export share figures conflict: 56% (AR2025 p.6; RATING), ~55% (CALL May 2025), 55.4% from the geography note (AR2025 p.167), 'more than two-third' in the risk note (AR2025 p.209), and foreign-exchange earnings of Rs1,376.35 crore (AR2025 p.41), which is [E] ~61% of FY25 revenue. These are not reconciled.

items: [F] Net unhedged USD exposure Rs269.99 crore and EUR exposure Rs13.86 crore at March 2025 (RATING); no forward contracts were outstanding at March 2025 versus US$6.13 million a year earlier (AR2025 p.209).
[F] Foreign-exchange gains of Rs19.23 crore were booked in FY25 other income (AR2025 p.160).
[F] The US announced a 26% reciprocal tariff on Indian imports in April 2025 (AR2025 p.79); CARE states ATBS is exempt from the recent US tariffs and expects a negligible impact (RATING, 6 Oct 2025).
[MC] The Iran war from February 2026 disrupted IBB raw materials; supply and logistics are now stable (CALL May 2026).

blocks.text: [F] All manufacturing is in Maharashtra: three sites at Mahad (Raigad) and one at Lote (Ratnagiri) (AR2025 p.13), with no international plants (AR2025 p.92). [AI] A regional event (flood, regulatory action, port disruption) could affect most output simultaneously; business-interruption cover is not disclosed beyond a statement that assets are 'properly insured' (AR2025 p.39).

[F] No case studies are disclosed. [F] CARE states the company has long-term contracts for IBB and ATBS with these clients (RATING); [MC] management refers to 'contracts in place' passing through raw material changes (CALL Aug 2024) and aims for annual and biannual AO contracts (CALL May 2025). [F] Contract tenors, volumes and take-or-pay terms are not disclosed.

[AI] Shown one way, concentration is low: no customer reaches 10% of revenue (AR2025 p.209). [AI] Shown the other way, it is high at the product and end-market level: ATBS is about one-third of revenue [MC] (CALL May 2026) and sold to a handful of global polymer makers, so a few buyers likely account for a large share of ATBS volume. [AI] Without top-5/top-10 disclosure the trend cannot be measured; product concentration is improving slowly as AO and IB grow, but that growth is in more competitive lines.
